messages:
support_alex: FYI - Customer 'AcmePayments' opened a P1: sustained 429s + 300-700ms tail latency on their Dedicated pool. They say it started after a maintenance window, around 14:12 UTC. I can reproduce 429s from their tenant id. Request ID sample: req_0a1b2c3d.

sam_oncall: Can you paste the exact error + a quick curl repro? Also which pool are they pinned to?

support_alex: Repro (from our side):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxx"\
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-payments"\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-*-redwood", "input":"hi"}'
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":"throttled: pool-cold-12 exceeded qps"}

Their Dedicated pool shows CPU/GPU low but token-level throttling. UI shows they were routed to `pool-cold-12` (cold capacity) instead of their reserved `pool-warm-42`.

jordan_runtime: That smells like a routing decision flip. Any recent control-plane deploys? I saw a routing rule change last night that touched tier labels.

maria_sre: @jordan_runtime yep, last deploy updated the routing parser to support comma-separated headers (PR #4321). I flagged a test mismatch but it merged for rollout. Could be the header parsing regressed mapping of `x-routing-tier` -> `tier` label.

support_alex: I grabbed control-plane logs for the request id (req_0a1b2c3d):
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:08Z] route_decision: tenant=acme-payments header.x-routing-tier="premium"
[2026-03-15T14:12:08Z] routing_match: failed to match pool with label tier=premium
[2026-03-15T14:12:08Z] fallback: selected pool=pool-cold-12 reason=fallthrough to cheapest
[2026-03-15T14:12:08Z] throttle: pool=pool-cold-12 tokens=0
```

sam_oncall: Interesting - header contains `premium` but match failed. Could be label name mismatch (e.g., `priority` vs `tier`) or parser trimming. Can someone run a quick control-plane query to show pool labels?

jordan_runtime: Running:
```
GET /controlplane/v1/pools?tenant=acme-payments
```
returns:
```
[{"id":"pool-warm-42","labels":{"priority":"premium","mode":"dedicated"}}, {"id":"pool-cold-12","labels":{"tier":"standard","mode":"shared"}}]
```
So pool-warm-42 uses `priority` key, but routing logic expected `tier`. The parser change may have renamed header->label mapping key to `tier`. That explains fallthrough.

liz_product: Customer claims they were pinned to `pool-warm-42`. Why did routing even evaluate header? Should have been tenant-pinned route.

maria_sre: Good catch — tenant pinning is supposed to be first precedence. Logs show tenant_pin lookup returned null at 14:12:07 due to a memcache miss (we had a brief memcached eviction during the same maintenance). So routing fell back to label-based rules. With label mismatch, it hit cheapest fallback and then throttle. Two failures combined.

support_alex: So root cause: (1) memcache eviction removed tenant->pool pin, (2) routing parser change caused header->label mapping to look for `tier` but pools used `priority`, causing mismatch and fallback to cold pool -> throttling.

jordan_runtime: Short-term mitigation: rewarm memcache for acme-payments and create a tenant->pool override to pin them to pool-warm-42. I can also roll back PR #4321 in the routing-parser to restore previous mapping.

sam_oncall: Agreed. Steps:
- jordan: run memcache write for tenant pin (done)
- support_alex: confirm if 429s cleared after pin
- maria_sre: revert parser change to staging and prepare hotfix for canary if reproduces

support_alex: After pin applied at 14:20 UTC, customer reports 429s dropped to zero, tail latency back to normal. Verified with curl -> 200 and normal token rates.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered rollback: PR #4321 reverted in control-plane (canary) at 14:32 UTC.

jordan_runtime: Follow-up fixes:
- tighten tenant-pin precedence so memcache miss falls back to DB read synchronously for pinned tenants (short TTL while we heal memcache)
- add defensive mapping: accept both `tier` and `priority` label keys when resolving header mappings
- add unit/regression test covering comma-separated headers + existing mapping keys

maria_sre: Also want to adjust autoscaler smoothing. We noticed autoscaler downscaled warm pools aggressively during the maintenance window because it used a 1m window on `token_throughput` which spiked low; change to 5m smoothing to avoid reactive scale-downs from brief noisy neighbor activity.

sam_oncall: I created ENG ticket: RUNTIME-8706 (routing fallback + parser mapping), SRE ticket: SRE-412 (memcache eviction hardening + autoscaler smoothing). Support notified customer and scheduled a 1:1 postmortem.

liz_product: Customer-facing note drafted: "We identified a combined routing and cache eviction issue that temporarily routed you to a cold pool; we pinned you to your reserved pool and deployed a rollback. We're adding extra checks to prevent recurrence and will follow up with a timeline for the permanent fix."

support_alex: Closing loop: customer accepted the note, monitoring is green. We'll include incident blameless postmortem and timeline for the hotfixes.

deploy-bot: canary rollback completed across 3 regions at 14:40 UTC.

sam_oncall: TL;DR: misrouted requests to cold pool due to memcache miss + routing parser mapping change -> temporary throttles. Mitigations: pin tenant, rollback parser change, add mapping acceptance and memcache hardening. Postmortem + follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
